description:
False-color satellite imagery from SPOT 5 (2.5 m resolution, 1/2/3 band combination) depicting a section of the Danube River and its floodplain within the Gemenc Ramsar Site, Hungary, captured on 2011-02-24. The image is a false-color composite where vegetation, likely forests and agricultural fields, appears in shades of magenta and red, while bare soil or sparse vegetation appears in lighter cyan/blue-green tones. Water bodies, including the main river channel and associated oxbow lakes, are depicted in dark blue.

Key features include:
*   A wide, meandering main river channel (Danube) running vertically along the right side of the image, appearing dark blue.
*   Numerous water bodies in the floodplain, including large, elongated dark blue oxbow lakes and meanders, particularly prominent to the left of the main channel. One distinct C-shaped oxbow is visible in the lower-middle left.
*   Extensive areas of dense vegetation, likely floodplain forests, appearing in very dark red, often bordering the water bodies and main river.
*   Agricultural fields are visible as large, rectangular or irregular patches in varying shades of magenta, pink, and cyan.
*   Scattered clusters of small, grey/purplish specks indicate built-up areas or settlements, particularly in the upper-left, middle-left, and lower-left sections, as well as along riverbanks.
The imagery was acquired by CNES 2011© and distributed by Airbus DS/Spot Image.
